units.translation: 301 cf. 423 ⟦1⟧ of hell. Nowhere in your spirit shall joy find a place, any more than in hell.
⟦1⟧ recalls 266 ⟦2⟧, and cf. ⟦3⟧ of the ⟦4⟧: ⟦5⟧ (Stanley for -⟦6⟧) ⟦7⟧. Weil's punctuation is: ⟦8⟧, ⟦9⟧, ⟦10⟧, so that ⟦11⟧ and ⟦12⟧ belong together and are separated by the explanation of ⟦13⟧.
may I be carried as food of a bitter drink

⟦1⟧ will thus be correct, without indication of which ⟦2⟧ they are, since the context points to the Erinyes themselves; so 22 f. ⟦3⟧, ⟦4⟧ . . ⟦5⟧, and 801 ⟦6⟧. But the trailing ⟦7⟧ is unpleasant and also stems only from Heath, while ⟦8⟧ is transmitted (also Schol.). This now can be ⟦9⟧, and the dative can belong to ⟦10⟧, like ⟦11⟧ in Pindar and other such things (Kühner-Gerth I, 428); cf. ⟦12⟧ ⟦13⟧, ⟦14⟧ ⟦15⟧. And if now ⟦16⟧ is also written, the connection of these words is clear, and it refers to the fact that even in Hades the Erinyes will not leave the criminal in peace: ⟦17⟧ 340.
nor may you cause barrenness by sending drops of the gods
and when dead he is not very free

303 ff. Also in what follows the tradition cannot be got through well. If one writes (Paley, Weil now): ⟦1⟧ (so also Schol.) ⟦2⟧, ⟦3⟧, ⟦4⟧; ⟦5⟧., that gives no good connection, and the sense: "what? you do not even say anything to this, but despise our words?" is little clearly expressed, since ⟦6⟧ would rather have to refer to ⟦7⟧ and mean "your words". Thus very good and very easy Weil earlier: ⟦8⟧; (which refers to Orestes' just heard speech); then can follow: ⟦9⟧ (-⟦10⟧) ⟦11⟧, ⟦12⟧ . . ⟦13⟧, ⟦14⟧., i.e. "but you will yourself abhor your impudent words, under the pain that we inflict on you for them". On ⟦15⟧ cf. passages like ⟦16⟧; on ⟦17⟧ ⟦18⟧. ⟦19⟧ etc., but especially ⟦20⟧ Ddf. ⟦21⟧ (Hippolytus Phaedra's proposals). - V.
and living you will feast on me etc.
